notes:
Summary: IronHarbor is a global litigation support firm building a single pane RAG search for compliance and discovery. Primary ask: private/VPC deployment with strong audit trail and retention for regulatory e-discovery holds. Technical scope: ingest ~18M raw documents (expected ~70M vectors after chunking & multi-granularity passageing). Workload: mix of high-throughput embeddings lookups (metadoc retrieval) and learned reranking for final results. Targets & constraints:
- Latency: end-to-end interactive search target <= 1s (p95 target < 900ms; current mid-POC p95 ~760ms). Reranker p99 < 400ms is a hard ask for certain flows.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 qps, burst up to 800 qps during rolling e-discovery events.
- Cost targets: aggregated cost per full query (retrieve+embed+rerank) target <$0.02 — procurement very price sensitive.
- Indexing: incremental reindexing cadence daily; nearline archive (cold store) must be queryable for legal holds.
- Data & security: VPC-only plane, customer-managed KMS/HSM, SSO via Okta (SAML), audit logs shipped to customer's SIEM with 7+ year retention and immutable audit export for e-discovery.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II required; ISO27001 preferred; evidence/attestation needed for procurement.
POC specifics & learnings: 
- POC ingestion pipeline validated at 30k docs/min for small files; large PDF parsing & OCR still outstanding on a subset (RD-6784).
- Two-stage retrieval architecture (sparse first-pass + dense embedding retrieval + learned reranker) best tradeoff for cost/latency — reducing candidate set before rerank lowered cost by ~35% in tests.
- Caching policies: prefix/KV caching for common queries reduces calls to reranker on repeated queries; exploring per-tenant memory cache in Dedicated cluster.
- Quantization: customer open to int8 quantization on reranker models but needs accuracy validation on regulatory prompts.
Stakeholders: CTO Daria Voss (technical lead), Head of Discovery Ops Aaron Steele (product champion), InfoSec lead Priya Nair (security), Procurement lead Simon Rhodes.
Quotes/attributions: "We need an auditable chain of custody for every returned result — legal will not accept fuzzy logs" (Priya Nair). "If you can keep cost per searched matter under our threshold we can consider 3-year reserved capacity" (Simon Rhodes).
Open items: final pricing for 3-year reserved capacity vs consumption model, KMS/HSM architecture diagram, SIEM integration test (log format + sample events), retention & legal-hold export API behavior.
